title: A zener regulator that survives
story: A 12 V adapter must give a small 5.1 V circuit (it behaves like a 1 kohm load) a steady supply. You have a 5.1 V zener diode rated 0.5 W but you only want it to run cool (under 0.1 W), and quarter-watt resistors. Pick the series resistor so the output stays between 4.9 V and 5.3 V, the zener stays under 0.1 W and the resistor under 0.25 W.
hints: The resistor carries the load current plus the zener current: I = (12 - 5.1) / R.
The load needs 5.1 mA. If the resistor can't supply that, the zener stops conducting and the output falls.
Whatever the load does not take goes through the zener and heats it: P = 5.1 V x I_zener.
